description: CUSTFILE OPEN, then a keyed READ that misses. app/cbl/CBSTM03B.CBL:118 EVALUATE LK-M03B-DD reaches WHEN 'CUSTFILE' at :123 - the THIRD dispatch arm, so the ordered dispatch is exercised past 'TRNXFILE' (:119) and 'XREFFILE' (:121) before :124 performs 3000-CUSTFILE-PROC THRU 3999-EXIT. Call one takes IF M03B-OPEN (:183) true: OPEN INPUT CUST-FILE (:184), GO TO 3900-EXIT (:185), and :200-201 MOVE CUSTFILE-STATUS TO LK-M03B-RC, so a successful OPEN INPUT reports '00' - on CUSTFILE-STATUS specifically, the third of the four independent two-byte status areas at :83-97, which is what a per-DD status assertion means. Call two takes IF M03B-READ-K (:188): MOVE LK-M03B-KEY (1:LK-M03B-KEY-LN) TO FD-CUST-ID and READ CUST-FILE INTO LK-M03B-FLDT (:189-190), driven exactly as app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:368-377 drives it, where :374 COMPUTE WS-M03B-KEY-LN = LENGTH OF XREF-CUST-ID makes the length 9 - pinned as the signed zoned image '000I', and as '000{' for the OPEN's zero, because PIC S9(4) overpunches its sign into the low-order byte rather than occupying a fifth one. Key 000000099 names none of the three seeded customers, so the read misses and CUSTFILE-STATUS carries '23'. The subroutine neither abends nor throws: it reports the status and hands back LK-M03B-FLDT exactly as it arrived, which here is the 1000 spaces the caller established with MOVE SPACES TO WS-M03B-FLDT at CBSTM03A:376. Deciding what '23' means belongs to the caller, and the two callers are deliberately asymmetric: the OPEN at CBSTM03A:783-799 accepts '00' OR '04', while the keyed read at :379-386 accepts only '00' and sends anything else to WHEN OTHER, DISPLAY 'ERROR READING CUSTFILE' and 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM. Keeping that decision there is the parity requirement - CBSTM03B has no DISPLAY of its own and never assigns RETURN-CODE, which is why the expected return code is 0 and no message is expected. CUSTFILE is ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM (:45), so 3000-CUSTFILE-PROC guards M03B-OPEN, M03B-READ-K and M03B-CLOSE and has no IF M03B-READ at all, unlike the two SEQUENTIAL DDs; all four SELECTs are OPEN INPUT and no paragraph writes, so the three seeded rows are read back unchanged as the read-only proof. The record decodes through app/cpy/CUSTREC.cpy (statement.model.Stm03CustomerRecord) and never through app/cpy/CVCUS01Y.cpy - CBSTM03A copies CUSTREC at :55 and moves LK-M03B-FLDT into that CUSTOMER-RECORD at :388 - so the date field pinned by name here is CUST-DOB-YYYYMMDD, not CVCUS01Y's CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD. The two layouts are byte-identical and differ in exactly that one field name, they are kept apart so field-for-field diffing stays meaningful, and using the wrong name is a difference. The seeded rows are a full 500 bytes with CUSTREC's trailing FILLER X(168) already space-filled on disk, so no normalisation applies - the only two in the whole suite are cardxref 36->50 and USRSEC 57->80, and neither concerns this DD. 'W' and 'Z' remain declared at :107-108 and are never SET anywhere in app/cbl, so this case does not drive them and preserving them unexercised is deliberate. Provenance: every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED - from those line numbers, from the CUSTREC offsets 9+25+25+25+50+50+50+2+3+10+15+15+9+20+10+10+1+3+168 = 500, from the LK-M03B-AREA widths 8+1+2+25+4+1000 = 1040 at :100-112, and from the real bytes of app/data/ASCII/custdata.txt rows 9 to 11 - and was never captured from an execution of the COBOL. Section 0.7.6 of the plan records eight independently verified blockers to running it here, and 0.9.11 escalates the substituted provenance as risk R-A; the 20 cases per program, the field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-zero gate are unchanged. HOW THE CALL SCRIPT IS DECLARED RATHER THAN HELD IN JAVA: the sequence of CALLs below used to live in a Java switch over this file's case identifier, which meant the case file did not describe the one thing it asserts - a subroutine whose entire contract is a DD name plus a one-character operation code IS its call sequence. Renumbering this file would have silently given it a different script, and a twenty-first case would have thrown from a default arm. unitStimulus.operationScript now carries it, one entry per CALL in issue order, each declaring LK-M03B-DD, the 88-level operation code from app/cbl/CBSTM03B.cbl:103-108, and where applicable LK-M03B-KEY and LK-M03B-KEY-LN. Two caller idioms are declared explicitly because the source distinguishes them: status '00' is the MOVE ZERO TO WS-M03B-RC every real call site issues, and its ABSENCE carries the previous call's status forward - the only way to observe a fall-through exit that assigns nothing new; primesRecordArea true is the MOVE SPACES TO WS-M03B-FLDT that app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:L350, :L745 and :L834 issue, and its ABSENCE is the omission at :L857-860 that makes 'at end of file the record area is returned unchanged' an assertion with content. Every expected area image below was derived from this script by reading CBSTM03B's rules, never by running the Java.
